meta.title: Squad: manager–worker coordination
meta.subtitle: Local CLI invocations coordinate through persisted tasks and mailboxes — not a manager daemon.

components.label: Manager terminal
components.explanation: The manager is an agent following role instructions, not an embedded scheduler. It checks agents, creates tracked assignments, and reads replies. Use task list to inspect completed task state; freeform replies use send/receive. Inspector review is role guidance and is outside this focused two-agent overview.

components.label: squad CLI
components.explanation: Each invocation locates an ancestor .squad directory and opens .squad/messages.db. Join registers an active agent, writes its session token, and prints role instructions. Mutating agent commands check active identity and session state. Receive returns text or JSON. With --wait it polls every 500 ms, refreshes last_seen every 30 s, and returns on delivery or timeout (default 3600 s).

components.label: Worker terminal
components.explanation: The worker executes the actual work outside Squad. For tracked work it receives the task_assigned message, explicitly acknowledges the task, then completes it with a summary. It can separately send a manager reply. Reading an assignment is not an acknowledgement, and task completion alone does not send a result message.

components.label: Role instructions
components.explanation: init copies built-in role prompts into the workspace. Join reads the custom role file if present, otherwise uses compiled-in defaults, and prints it. These files guide agent behavior; they are not an enforced manager-only authorization policy.

components.label: Store / SQL operations
components.explanation: create_task atomically inserts a queued task and task_assigned message, requiring active creator and assignee. ack_task requires queued status and matching assignee, and records a 15-minute lease. complete_task requires acked status and matching lease owner; it persists the summary but neither checks lease expiry nor sends a message. receive_messages selects unread messages and marks those rows read in one transaction. requeue_task clears lease/result and optionally assigns an active agent; it sends no assignment message.

components.label: Local coordination files
components.explanation: Join writes the session token file; validation compares it with the expected database token. Missing files are accepted for backward compatibility, so this is not a strong authentication boundary. receive --wait holds an exclusive fs2 file lock at workspace-root locks/<agent>.receive.lock for the duration of the wait; non-wait receives do not take that lock.

components.label: SQLite: messages.db
components.explanation: One shared local database persists agent identity, role, session token, client metadata and presence; task assignment, status, lease and result; and message sender/recipient, unread flag, kind, task_id and reply_to. Tasks and mailboxes are distinct state: reading messages changes read flags, not task status. Only Store executes SQL; agent terminals communicate through CLI invocations rather than direct peer transport.

cards.title: Assignment → execution → observation
items: Create commits queued task + unread task_assigned together; both agents must be active.
Receive marks mail read; ack separately moves queued → acked for the assigned worker.
Complete moves acked → completed for the lease owner. Manager reads task list, or worker separately sends a reply.

cards.title: Mailbox is not task state
items: send / receive is the freeform fallback; direct notes can carry task_id and reply_to. @all fans out to other active agents (src/main.rs:706–734; src/store.rs:317–374).
Task assignment output joins the task body/status onto its message; --json emits envelopes (src/main.rs:487–580).
Read marking commits before output is printed: do not infer end-to-end processing acknowledgement.

cards.title: Boundaries and implementation limits
items: Roles are prompts, not manager-only permissions. External agent execution and inspector review are omitted.
Ack records a 15-minute lease; complete does not enforce expiry. Requeue is explicit and emits no message (src/store.rs:13,624–718).
Shared local workspace only in this path: no evidenced daemon, push channel, automatic result delivery, or automatic expired-lease recovery.
